extracted.intended_audience: Arts organizations, small nonprofit arts groups, researchers, state and regional arts agencies, and applicants seeking NEA funding
extracted.subtask_short: NEA grants application guidance for organizations
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of National Endowment for the Arts (NEA) grant programs, eligibility, deadlines, and post-award compliance resources for organizations and researchers applying for NEA funding. Includes descriptions of principal grant categories and program-specific targeting (e.g., small organizations, creative placemaking, research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants for Arts Projects (GAP) — principal grants category
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants for Arts Projects (GAP) is our principal grants category, providing project-based funding for organizations. Grants are available for arts projects of all sizes in a wide variety of artistic disciplines. Projects may take place in any part of the nation’s 50 states, the District of Columbia, and U.S. jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines: February 12, 2026, and July 9, 2026. Applicants (first-time or returning) should read funding guidelines to understand the types of projects NEA is particularly interested in funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Our Town (creative placemaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Town supports creative placemaking arts projects in communities across the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To simplify intake and review, Our Town applicants apply within the Grants for Arts Projects (GAP) program and choose the 'Design & Our Town' discipline. Applications are accepted at the February or July 2026 deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge America (small organization grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge America provides $10,000 grants for arts projects from small organizations (less than $250,000 in prior year operating expenses) that extend the reach of the arts to underserved groups/communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To simplify intake and review, Challenge America applicants apply within the Grants for Arts Projects (GAP) program and choose the 'Challenge America' discipline. Applications are accepted at the February or July 2026 deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership Agreement Grants (SAAs and RAOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are awarded to the nation’s state and jurisdictional arts agencies (SAAs), and the regional arts organizations (RAOs) whose members comprise SAAs. Partnership support is also available to the national service organization for the state arts agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Grants in the Arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Grants in the Arts supports research studies that investigate the value and/or impact of the arts in American life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of two NEA research funding opportunities. *Deadline has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEA Research Labs
rubrics_metrics.description: NEA Research Labs fund long-term research agendas that include empirical studies and the dissemination of products or services for promoting public knowledge about the arts and their contributions to American life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant type: organizations (general eligibility expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEA grant programs described on this page are primarily project-based funding for organizations (including small organizations and state/regional arts agencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both first-time and returning applicants are welcomed; applicants should consult program-specific guidelines for detailed eligibility rules and any organization-size thresholds (e.g., Challenge America definition of 'small').

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These deadlines apply to Grants for Arts Projects and the associated disciplines (e.g., Our Town, Challenge America). Some programs or cycles (e.g., Partnership Agreement Grants, specific research opportunities) may have had deadlines that have passed—check program pages for current cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope of projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects may take place in any part of the nation’s 50 states, the District of Columbia, and U.S. jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure project activities occur within the NEA's eligible geographic jurisdictions or consult program guidance for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage Your Award — post-award compliance and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage Your Award is for recipients of offers and awards from the National Endowment for the Arts and provides guidance necessary to understand and comply with the rules, regulations, and policies that govern your federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes all forms and instructions needed to manage the award from offer to closeout; recipients must follow these rules and complete required forms to remain in compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Time Applicant Guide for Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance specifically for organizations applying to the NEA for the first time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to help first-time applicants understand every step of the grantmaking process; NEA staff strive to ensure applicants receive the support they need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer to be a Panelist (reviewer participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunity and invitation to serve as an application reviewer: 'Want to serve as an application reviewer? Volunteer to be a Panelist.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates NEA uses panels of reviewers and accepts volunteer panelists; consult the volunteer/panelist page for selection criteria, qualifications, and expectations for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and regional funding information (SAAs and RAOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find out more about funding opportunities available through your state arts agency and regional arts organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may pursue complementary or alternative funding through state arts agencies and regional arts organizations; NEA encourages coordination with these entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recent Grants as program exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about NEA grants awarded since 1998.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use past awarded projects to understand the types, scales, and geographic distribution of projects NEA funds; consult Recent Grants to identify examples relevant to your application.
